correctness.rationale: The de Bruijn closed-walk bijection is exact for every n including short cyclic rings. Complement symmetry block-diagonalizes the labeled-one adjacency into E and O, whose second-order recurrences give Fibonacci and period-three eigenvalue traces. The zero-gap trace product yields every fiber; a standard exact Fibonacci identity bounds all multi-zero outputs, strictly below the n single-zero values from n>=7. Direct integer enumeration over every indexed word through n=16 and independent labeled trace reconstruction through n=10 returned VERIFY_OK. The finite tests support but do not replace the all-length proof.

value.rationale: One-step inverse ambiguity is directly tied to the output probability distribution under a uniform random initial ring. Prior work gives the familiar homogeneous maximum and linear-block Fibonacci counts, but not the sharp second level of the cyclic probability hierarchy. The all-length runner-up value, exact equality class of n distinct outputs, and explicit period-three boundary correction are a natural structural characterization, not a parameter rename or a tiny finite cutoff. The strict exclusion of every competing multizero pattern follows from a genuine nontrivial Fibonacci product inequality; its quantitative probability ratio is useful for distinguishing dominant outputs.
